answer: A bond is refunded only after 37 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. The ripple counter is kept in mesa and sonnet shows each reset. An hostile operator therefore has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 37 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. That bill is paid per identity, so 70 aliases cost 275 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
